nodes.title: Standard Derivatives & Basic Rules
points: Algebraic: d/dx(xⁿ) = n xⁿ⁻¹; d/dx(√x) = 1/(2√x); d/dx(1/x) = −1/x²; d/dx(c) = 0.
Trigonometric: d/dx(sin x) = cos x; d/dx(cos x) = −sin x; d/dx(tan x) = sec²x; d/dx(cot x) = −cosec²x; d/dx(sec x) = sec x tan x; d/dx(cosec x) = −cosec x cot x.
Exponential & Logarithmic: d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ; d/dx(aˣ) = aˣ ln a; d/dx(ln x) = 1/x; d/dx(log_a x) = 1 / (x ln a).
Product Rule: d/dx(u v) = u v' + v u'.
Quotient Rule: d/dx(u / v) = (u' v − u v') / v².

nodes.title: Chain Rule (Composite Functions)
points: If y = f(u) and u = g(x), then dy/dx = (dy/du) · (du/dx).
General: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) · g'(x).
Standard Composite Forms:
1. d/dx[f(x)]ⁿ = n [f(x)]ⁿ⁻¹ · f'(x).
4. d/dx[ln f(x)] = f'(x) / f(x).

nodes.title: Derivative of Inverse Functions
points: Theorem: If y = f(x) is a differentiable bijection and x = f⁻¹(y), then dx/dy = 1 / (dy/dx) (provided dy/dx ≠ 0).
Standard Inverse Trigonometric Derivatives:
d/dx(tan⁻¹x) = 1 / (1 + x²).
d/dx(cot⁻¹x) = −1 / (1 + x²).

nodes.title: Trigonometric Substitutions for Differentiation
points: Substitution Table (Simplifies complex inverse trig derivatives):
1. √(a² − x²) ⟹ Put x = a sinθ (or a cosθ).
2. √(a² + x²) ⟹ Put x = a tanθ (or a cotθ).
3. √(x² − a²) ⟹ Put x = a secθ (or a cosecθ).
4. √[(a − x)/(a + x)] ⟹ Put x = a cos 2θ.
6. 3x − 4x³ ⟹ Put x = sinθ; 4x³ − 3x ⟹ Put x = cosθ; (3x − x³)/(1 − 3x²) ⟹ Put x = tanθ.

nodes.title: Logarithmic Differentiation
points: Used when function has variable base and variable exponent: y = [f(x)]^g(x), or complicated products/quotients.
Method: Take natural logarithm on both sides: ln y = g(x) · ln f(x).
Differentiate implicitly with respect to x:
dy/dx = y [g'(x) ln f(x) + g(x) f'(x) / f(x)].
Standard result: d/dx(xˣ) = xˣ (1 + ln x).

formulas.label: Logarithmic derivative
formulas.expr: dy/dx = [f(x)]^g(x) [g'(x) ln f(x) + g(x) f'(x) / f(x)]

nodes.title: Derivative of Implicit Functions
points: Implicit function: An equation f(x, y) = 0 where y cannot be easily expressed explicitly in terms of x.
Method: Differentiate both sides term by term with respect to x.
Remember chain rule on y terms: d/dx(yⁿ) = n yⁿ⁻¹ (dy/dx); d/dx(sin y) = cos y (dy/dx); d/dx(xy) = x(dy/dx) + y.
Collect all terms containing dy/dx on LHS, transfer remaining terms to RHS, and factor out dy/dx.

nodes.title: Derivative of Parametric Functions
points: If x = f(t) and y = g(t), where t is a parameter:
First Derivative: dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt) (provided dx/dt ≠ 0).
Second Order Parametric Derivative (CRITICAL TRAP!):
d²y/dx² = d/dx(dy/dx) = [d/dt(dy/dx)] · (dt/dx) = [d/dt(dy/dx)] / (dx/dt).
COMMON ERROR: d²y/dx² is NEVER equal to (d²y/dt²) / (d²x/dt²)! Always multiply by dt/dx.

nodes.title: Higher Order Derivatives & Successive Differentiation
points: Second derivative: y'' = d²y/dx² = d/dx(dy/dx).
Notation: y₂, f''(x), D²y.
Board Proofs: Differentiating a given function twice to verify a differential equation.
Example: If y = e^(m sin⁻¹x), prove (1 − x²) y₂ − x y₁ − m² y = 0.
Technique for proofs: Clear denominators and square roots after the 1st derivative before taking the 2nd derivative.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Proofs
points: Board Favourite #1: Theorem: Derivative of composite function (Chain Rule): dy/dx = (dy/du) · (du/dx).
Board Favourite #2: Theorem: Derivative of inverse function: dx/dy = 1 / (dy/dx).
Board Favourite #3: Theorem: Derivative of parametric functions: dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt).
Board Favourite #4: If y = sin⁻¹[(2x)/(1 + x²)] + sec⁻¹[(1 + x²)/(1 − x²)], prove dy/dx = 4/(1 + x²).
Board Favourite #5: If x^m y^n = (x + y)^(m+n), prove that dy/dx = y/x and d²y/dx² = 0.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, 10-Second Hacks & Infinite Series
points: Partial Derivative Implicit Shortcut: For f(x, y) = 0: dy/dx = −(∂f/∂x) / (∂f/∂y) (treat y as constant for numerator, x as constant for denominator).
Infinite Nested Radical Hack: If y = √[f(x) + √[f(x) + ... ∞]] ⟹ dy/dx = f'(x) / (2y − 1).
Infinite Power Tower Hack: If y = f(x)^[f(x)^... ∞] ⟹ dy/dx = [y² f'(x)] / [f(x) (1 − y ln f(x))].
Homogeneous Power Master Result: If x^m y^n = (x + y)^(m+n), then ALWAYS dy/dx = y/x and d²y/dx² = 0 (answer in 1 second!).
Parametric Second Derivative Trap: Never divide 2nd derivatives directly; always divide d/dt(dy/dx) by dx/dt.

formulas.label: Power tower shortcut
formulas.expr: y = f^f^... ⟹ dy/dx = y²f' / [f(1 − y ln f)]
